clue.text: Pouches for Dickens's Herbert and Matthew

parts.note: describes the revolving three-sided prism used in ancient Greek theatre to switch scenery

parts.note: points to the poet who told of a band of pilgrims riding to Canterbury, nodding at Bunyan's title

explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury Tales follows pilgrims on their journey, so its poet chronicled their progress.

clue.text: A friend of Tom Brown, and one of Gulley Jimson, seen in Eliot's west country village

parts.note: Harry East is Tom's schoolfriend in Tom Brown's School Days
Coker is the barmaid who befriends Gulley Jimson in Joyce Cary's The Horse's Mouth

explanation.surface: Two fictional companions turn up in a Somerset village a poet wrote about.
explanation.walkthrough: East Coker is a Somerset village and the title of the second of T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets.
explanation.definitionFit: The village in Somerset gives its name to one of Eliot's Four Quartets, where his ashes lie.

parts.note: unhappy means sad

explanation.surface: A gloomy aristocrat from the East tries his hand at fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: The notorious French nobleman wrote novels such as Justine, so he was a marquis turned writer.

parts.note: the French word for a Romani person is the title of Ravel's rhapsody for violin

explanation.definitionFit: Ravel's virtuoso violin rhapsody takes its title from the French word for a Romani musician.

clue.text: Thanksgiving, for example, from Ben Travers

definitions.meaning: a festive season when the roast bird is served, like Christmas
a title among Ben Travers's Aldwych farces of the 1930s

explanation.definitionFit: Holidays centred on a roast bird are jokily called that season, and Travers used the phrase for a farce.

clue.text: Anger about publicity for sultan's decree

parts.note: anger means ire
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Fury over press coverage greets an Ottoman ruler's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A written order issued by an Ottoman ruler was known by this Turkish word.

clue.text: Discreet scenarios to conceal name of poet

indicators.note: the words scenarios to conceal, or hold within them, the poet's name

explanation.surface: Tactful plot outlines keep an author's identity secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'scenARIOS TO'; 'Discreet' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovico Ariosto was the Italian Renaissance author of Orlando Furioso.

parts.note: any painter needs a stand for the canvas, with a hint at relief for one hard up

explanation.definitionFit: Painters rest a canvas on this wooden stand while working, so it is support an artist needs.

parts.note: points to O. Henry's story collection titled after paths of destiny

explanation.definitionFit: O. Henry's 1909 collection was titled after the routes of destiny a character might take.

parts.note: the speaker of this line is the servant Brutus asks to kill him at Philippi

parts.note: the poet Anne Stevenson titled a 1969 collection after setbacks or turnarounds

clue.text: Public school alumnus, less recognize able than Icarus

indicators.note: made harder to recognise, so the letters of the two words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old boy of some school is harder to identify than the boy who flew too near the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: An old Charterhouse boy is called this, after the school's Carthusian monastery origins; Charterhouse is an English private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Former pupils of Charterhouse school take the name from the Carthusian order whose priory the school replaced.

clue.text: Card game in a Nigerian language

definitions.meaning: a central European game played with a tarot pack
a tongue spoken in Plateau State, Nigeria

explanation.definitionFit: Both a tarot-pack card game of Austria and a language of central Nigeria share this name.

a tomb is a final resting place

explanation.surface: Someone is told to move a grave, perhaps on behalf of a numbered friend.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is the answer to 2-down, the Canterbury poet, whose monument in Westminster Abbey is of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Westminster Abbey monument is a raised table-shaped tomb, the kind named for its resemblance to an altar.

definitions.meaning: rest means whatever is left over
an unsold copy that a publisher clears off cheaply

explanation.definitionFit: What is left over is the leftover part, and publishers sell surplus unsold stock at a discount under the same name.

clue.text: An MBA halo might be arranged for Carthaginian deity

indicators.note: these letters could be arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A business degree and a saintly ring could be organised for an ancient god.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the chief god of Carthage, worshipped by the Phoenician colonists of North Africa.

clue.text: Clumsily mar a set-up in offprint

indicators.note: done clumsily, so the following letters fall into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone awkwardly spoils an arrangement in a printed extract.
explanation.definitionFit: A separately printed copy of an article from a journal is called by this Latin term.

parts.note: before anyone goes on a trip, the suitcases must be filled, so a joke title precedes Henry Green's novel

explanation.definitionFit: Filling suitcases comes before setting off, so it would be the step before Party Going.

parts.note: Dashiell Hammett's statuette bird is named after an island in the Mediterranean

explanation.definitionFit: The jewelled falcon in Hammett's novel is named after the Mediterranean island, its supposed origin.

parts.note: the missing word completes Cowper's line about one who talks little and attends approvingly

clue.text: Plutarch's father of Sparta English by Dryden

parts.words: Plutarch's father of Sparta English by Dryden
parts.note: the Spartan lawgiver whose life Plutarch wrote, in the Lives translated under Dryden's name

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary lawgiver of Sparta is the subject of one of Plutarch's Lives, Englished in the Dryden translation.

definitions.meaning: the youngest Bennet sister in Pride and Prejudice
an ancient kingdom located in western Anatolia

explanation.definitionFit: Austen's youngest Bennet girl shares her name with the ancient kingdom of Croesus in western Anatolia.

parts.note: Schnitzler's play Reigen, a round dance of partners, is known in French by its circle-dance title

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a round dance titles Schnitzler's play, whose couples pass on like a children's ring game.

parts.note: Kit was Christopher Marlowe's familiar name, so his possessive gives Kit's

explanation.surface: The Elizabethan playwright's place of worship turns out to be nothing more than crowd-pleasing.

clue.text: Fairy queen I confuse in poetic measure

parts.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: A fairy monarch tells how she muddles a line of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of one unstressed then one stressed syllable is the basic unit of English verse.

parts.note: the hero's wives were Megara, then Omphale, then the princess of Calydon

explanation.definitionFit: Heracles' last wife, who unwittingly killed him with the poisoned shirt, came after Megara and Omphale.

parts.note: Grahame's 1898 book of childhood stories is titled with a word for reverie before days

clue.text: Storm god named sea and moon

definitions.text: Storm god named sea and moon

parts.words: Storm god named sea and moon
parts.note: a hundred-handed giant of Greek myth, linked to storms and the Aegean, whose name echoes that sea

explanation.definitionFit: The giant also called Briareus was a violent sea-storm deity whose name recalls the Aegean.

clue.text: Energy units in good French exponent of élan vital

indicators.note: in places the energy units within the French word for good

parts.note: bon is French for good
ergs are units of energy in the CGS system

explanation.surface: Physics units appear inside a French word for good, describing a philosopher of life force.
explanation.walkthrough: élan vital, the vital impulse, is the philosopher's own term; the French element is flagged only by the word French.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Bergson, the French philosopher, coined the phrase for the vital impulse driving evolution.
